skill.description: Guides proxychains4 setup and troubleshooting for routing selected network commands through a local proxy at 127.0.0.1:9910.
skill.summary: Configure and troubleshoot proxychains4 routing for command-line network access.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally automates proxychains4 use and contains persistent proxy configuration and shell setup guidance. Markdown backtick, entropy, device-file, and local port diagnostic hits are mostly false positives, but proxy routing, hidden configuration writes, proxy environment variables, and privileged installation guidance are real security concerns. Semantic review found automatic proxying of blocked or failed network commands that can bypass network controls without explicit user consent.

remediation.issue: Automatic proxy routing for blocked or failed network commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before adding proxychains4, especially for blocked access, authentication, production, or customer data traffic.

remediation.issue: Persistent hidden proxy configuration and wrapper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact files that will change, back up existing configuration, avoid shell startup edits by default, and provide rollback steps.

remediation.issue: Privileged package and system configuration commands
remediation.suggestion: Never auto-run sudo commands. Present them as manual steps with package source verification and user confirmation.
Ask before contacting external test services and allow users to configure an approved internal endpoint.

content.value_statement: Network commands can fail when access is blocked, slow, or limited by DNS. This skill provides proxychains4 guidance, configuration examples, and troubleshooting steps for routing selected commands through a local proxy.
actual_capabilities: Identifies timeout, DNS failure, connection refusal, and blocked access cases where proxychains4 may be relevant.
Shows proxychains4 command patterns for curl, git, pip, npm, wget, Docker, and SSH workflows.
Provides user-level proxychains.conf examples for a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:9910.
Includes a shell setup script that creates ~/.proxychains/proxychains.conf and tests proxy access.
Documents troubleshooting checks for proxy service status, DNS proxying, and configuration file permissions.
limitations: Requires proxychains4 and a trusted local proxy service to be installed and running.
Proxychains mainly supports TCP traffic from dynamically linked programs, not all network protocols.
The skill does not decide whether bypassing a network block is allowed by policy or law.
Some setup steps may modify user configuration files or require elevated package manager commands.

best_practices: Ask for explicit approval before routing any user command through a proxy.
Use only trusted proxy services and avoid sending secrets through unknown routes.
Document every configuration file change and keep a simple rollback path.
anti_patterns: Do not automatically proxy sensitive authentication, production, or customer data traffic.
Do not run package manager or system commands with elevated privileges without user approval.
Do not hide persistent proxy configuration changes from the user.

faq.question: Does this skill install proxychains4 by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance and a setup script, but elevated package commands should require user approval.

faq.question: What proxy address does the skill expect?
faq.answer: The examples use a local proxy at 127.0.0.1:9910 unless the user chooses a different trusted proxy.

faq.question: Can proxychains route every command?
faq.answer: No. It mainly supports TCP traffic from dynamically linked programs, and some applications may bypass it.

faq.question: Why is this skill security sensitive?
faq.answer: It can change network routing, use hidden user configuration files, and suggest privileged setup commands.

faq.question: Should it be used for blocked websites?
faq.answer: Only when the user confirms that proxy use complies with local policy, law, and service rules.

faq.question: How can users remove the configuration?
faq.answer: They can delete the user-level proxychains configuration and remove any shell aliases or wrapper scripts they created.
